core_obligations: Write M as a directed colimit of finitely presented modules and use that P is finitely presented to factor f through a single stage M_j (proof lines 21641-21643).
Tensor with Q and consider the image y of the given element x in the tensor product with M_j, which lies in the kernel of the map to the tensor product with M (proof lines 21644-21651).
Use that the tensor product with Q is the colimit of the tensor products with the M_i to find j' at least j where y already maps to zero, and take P' = M_{j'} (proof lines 21652-21656).
proof_roadmap: Factor the map from the finitely presented module through one stage of a colimit presentation of M (proof lines 21640-21643).
Push the vanishing of the element to a later stage using commutation of tensor products with colimits (proof lines 21644-21657).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finitely presented module P, a map f from P into M and an element x of the kernel after tensoring with Q, there is a finitely presented module P' through which f factors and in whose tensored kernel x still dies (statement lines 21631-21638). The proof does not estimate the size of the kernel: it presents M as a directed colimit of finitely presented modules, uses finite presentability of P to factor f through one stage, and then uses that tensoring commutes with the colimit to push the vanishing of the image of x to a later stage (proof lines 21640-21657). Finding the two stages, first for the map and then for the element, is the content, and the author writes both steps out. H2.
